stem: A client arrives in the PACU after general anesthesia. The client is very drowsy, is breathing spontaneously, and has oral secretions. There is no surgical or spinal restriction that prevents repositioning. Which nursing action best supports airway protection while the client is not fully alert?

options.A: Keep the client flat and supine regardless of secretions so that positioning does not influence the airway
options.B: Position the client laterally or turn the head to the side as clinically appropriate and keep suction available while continuing respiratory assessment
options.C: Place the client prone because prone positioning is required after general anesthesia
options.D: Sit the client fully upright immediately even if the client's level of consciousness does not allow safe maintenance of that position

rationale: In a markedly drowsy client without a positioning contraindication, lateral or head-turned positioning can help secretions drain away from the airway while the nurse continues close respiratory assessment and has suction available. Postanesthesia care remains individualized; no single position is appropriate for every surgical client.
educational_objective: Use individualized positioning and airway-support measures to reduce aspiration or obstruction risk in a drowsy postanesthesia client.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Postoperative Nursing Care — Phase I/PACU: close monitoring of airway and recovery indicators takes precedence as clients emerge from anesthesia
source_claim_supported: Airway assessment and protection are immediate priorities during postanesthesia recovery; positioning must be adapted to the client's clinical and surgical context.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — alterations in body systems / impaired ventilation and airway management
correction_summary: Removed the source's universal 'typical PACU position' wording. Added explicit no-positioning-contraindication context, spontaneous breathing, secretions, continued assessment, and suction availability to make the answer clinically bounded rather than absolute.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: NCBI perioperative care chapter checked; source supports airway priority but not a universal position for all clients.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Final item limits lateral/head-turn positioning to a drowsy spontaneously breathing client with secretions and no repositioning contraindication.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; supine positioning may worsen secretion pooling in this scenario.
audit_findings.choice_B: Correct; supports drainage/airway protection plus continued respiratory monitoring.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; prone positioning is not a universal PACU requirement.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; full upright positioning may be unsafe in a markedly drowsy client unable to maintain posture.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B addresses airway protection within the stated constraints.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation alignment strengthened from Basic Care and Comfort.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked surgical restrictions, spinal precautions, airway adjunct need, aspiration risk, and universal-position overclaim; stem explicitly excludes the main contraindication ambiguity.
